title: Remaker AI Face Swap: How It Works, Free Plan Limits, and Best Alternatives (2026)
summary: Use the official Remaker AI website and compare its free photo swap, video limits, one-time credit pricing, API, privacy details and alternatives.

## Quick answer


**The official Remaker AI website is remaker.ai; Remaker says it does not have an official mobile app.**


Its browser tools cover photo, video, GIF, batch and multi-face swaps. The[photo face-swap tool](https://remaker.ai/face-swap-free/) advertises no signup and no watermark. The[video face-swap tool](https://remaker.ai/video-face-swap-online/) displays one credit per second and supports uploads up to 500 MB or 30 minutes. Credit packs are one-time purchases, start at $5.99 for 200 credits, and do not expire according to Remaker's current site.


For another browser service in this category, see the[AIFaceSwap.io review](https://magichour.ai/blog/aifaceswapio-review) . Compare the exact photo or video workflow and its export allowance; similar service names do not imply shared accounts or credits.

## **What Is Remaker AI?**


[Remaker AI](http://remaker.ai/) is a browser-based AI editing platform that offers[face swapping](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap) ,[AI image generation](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-image-generator) , background removal, image upscaling, AI headshots, and dozens of other[creative tools](https://marketinglad.io/best-free-ai-art-generators/) .


Remaker uses a **pay-as-you-go credit system** with one-time purchases rather than a monthly subscription. Buy credits when the selected workflow and quote meet your needs.


Everything runs in the browser, making it accessible on both desktop and mobile devices without downloading software.


## Which official Remaker site should you use?


Start at[remaker.ai](https://remaker.ai/) for the service reviewed here. Remaker's[official app notice](https://remaker.ai/official-remaker-ai-app/) says it does not currently offer an official app and warns against similarly named App Store or Google Play listings. Use the browser site and do not assume that another app's login, purchases, privacy terms or developer belong to Remaker AI.


Before paying, match the developer, support destination, account, and billing terms to the service you intended to use. A third-party page displaying “Remaker AI” does not establish an official Remaker model or shared credits.

## **How Remaker AI Face Swap Works**


### 1. Open the appropriate Remaker tool


For a still image, go directly to[Remaker Photo Face Swap](https://remaker.ai/face-swap-free/) , which currently advertises no-signup, watermark-free access. For a moving clip, open[Video Face Swap](https://remaker.ai/video-face-swap-online/) ; its FAQ says purchasing credits unlocks VIP video access. Account signup offers are separate from those tool-specific rules. Screenshots below show an earlier account interface.


### **2. Open the Face Swap tool**


Choose the mode for your file: a single photo, multiple faces, video/GIF or batch processing. Use the current tool labels and generation quote rather than assuming every captured menu is unchanged.


### **3. Upload your photos**


In the current photo tool, upload the **Original Image** first: the scene whose face you want to replace. Then upload the **Target face** : the portrait supplying the new face. Read the helper text beneath each input; other services sometimes use “source” and “target” in the opposite order.


The current photo picker accepts **JPEG, PNG, WEBP and BMP** . If your phone photo uses another format, export a JPEG or PNG copy first; changing the filename extension does not convert it. Original Image is the scene receiving the swap, while Target face supplies the replacement identity. These formats come from the[official photo tool’s upload controls](https://remaker.ai/face-swap-free/) , checked October 10, 2026.


### 4. Check the available model and generation quote


The earlier interface screenshot shows V1 and V2 options. Those labels describe that captured version of the tool, not a guarantee about the controls currently available to every account.


For video, Remaker’s current tool shows Regular Swap and Face (HD) Swap. These are current video controls; the V1/V2 screenshot above shows an earlier interface. Compare the same short clip and replacement portrait, confirm the selected mode’s quote, and review moving frames before processing the full video.


### **5. Generate and download**


Click **Swap** and wait for processing to finish.


Inspect the actual download for a watermark and check the export conditions for your chosen tool. Photo and video offers can differ.


## Single face, multiple faces or batch: which Remaker mode?


Multiple faces means several people in one scene; batch means several source files. Remaker’s single-photo form explicitly directs group images to its separate[Multiple Face Swap tool](https://remaker.ai/multiple-face-swap/) . Upload the group photo there and supply the intended replacement portrait. Review every person in the downloaded image, including anyone who should remain unchanged.


Group video has an extra detection step. The official[Video Multi Face Swap interface](https://remaker.ai/video-multi-face-swap/) asks you to capture screenshots containing all the faces you intend to swap, then choose Detect Faces. Capture a clear frame for each intended person, add the replacement faces, select the clip range and confirm the assignments before generating. If a person never appears in the captured frames, revisit detection before spending credits on another attempt. This is the documented interface sequence, not a completed generation test.


*Remaker’s group-video interface, captured October 12, 2026: select Multiple Faces, upload a video or GIF, then detect the faces to replace. This shows the inputs and displayed quote, not a generated result.*[View the current interface](https://remaker.ai/video-multi-face-swap/)


For one replacement identity across many still images, the[batch tool’s Multiple Original Images mode](https://remaker.ai/features/batche-face-swap/) lists a maximum of 50 original images per session and a separate target-face upload. For example, twelve permitted portraits are a batch job; three people in one portrait are a multiple-face job. Start with one representative photo before submitting the remaining set. Confirm the current quote and review each output rather than assuming one successful result proves the whole batch.


For a browser comparison using the same group clip, open[Magic Hour Multiple Face Swap Video](https://magichour.ai/products/multiple-face-swap/video) . Use a short segment and assign the intended replacements before checking moving frames. Compare the selected route’s allowance and export conditions; a single-face trial does not establish group-video behavior.


### How to use Remaker on iPhone or Android


Remaker’s documented mobile photo workflow runs in a browser. Its[official photo FAQ](https://remaker.ai/face-swap-free/) names Safari on iPhone and Chrome or Firefox on Android. Open the official site, choose the photo or multiple-face route for the job, upload the original scene and replacement portrait, then inspect and download the result. This browser route does not require an APK installation; an unrelated app-store listing does not prove it is the same service.


Save the original media before switching tools or accounts. For a one-person mobile-browser comparison, use[Magic Hour Photo Face Swap](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap) with those originals. Compare the actual download on your phone, including identity, crop and watermark, rather than a compressed messaging-app copy.

**Worked example:** at the video tool’s displayed rate of **one credit per second** , one thirty-second attempt uses **30 credits** . At the 200-credit pack’s $5.99 price, that is about **$0.90 of purchased credits** , but the minimum purchase is still $5.99. Three attempts use 90 credits, leaving 110 from that pack. This is budget arithmetic, not a measured success rate; confirm the selected mode’s quote before generating.


**The selected mode changes the budget.** Remaker’s multi-face video page currently displays two credits per second. A thirty-second group-video attempt therefore uses 60 credits at that displayed rate, compared with 30 for regular single-face video. These are operation-cost calculations, not measured successful exports. Check the actual generation quote before starting. ## **Where Remaker AI Face Swap Falls Short**


- **Free access needs an account-specific check.** Confirm the balance, expiry, tool eligibility, and download restrictions shown to you.
- **A credit pack is not a fixed number of finished videos.** Duration, settings, and repeated attempts affect usage.
- **A completed swap still needs review.** Watch turns, expressions, and obstructions before paying to process a longer version.

### **2. DeepSwap**

[DeepSwap](https://www.deepswap.ai/) is designed primarily for video face swapping and supports replacing **up to six faces in a single video** , making it a strong choice for group videos, short films, and social media skits.


Compare a short sample containing the expressions and movements in your actual project before committing to a longer export.


[DeepSwap’s published rates](https://www.deepswap.ai/en/pricing) distinguish photos, GIFs and video. Its video rate is one credit per fifteen seconds, but DeepSwap credits and Remaker credits have different purchase prices. Compare the total cost and required export for the same clip.

**Best for:** replacing different faces in a small group photo or video.


[Pica AI](https://www.pica-ai.com/face-swap/) supports up to **three faces per photo or video** , with each reference assigned to a different original face. Its video workflow offers GIF or MP4 downloads. Check the current generation and download offer rather than relying on an old fixed daily quota.


## **Does Remaker AI have a face-swap API?**


Yes. Remaker publishes separate API documentation for photo face swap, multiple-face swap, and video face swap. The[photo face-swap API](https://remaker.ai/docs/api/face-swap/) uses an API key, documents a regular-user limit of 20 task submissions per minute, and says generated images are deleted after 24 hours. Confirm current pricing, limits, output retention, retries, and commercial terms for the exact endpoint before building a production workflow.

## Is Remaker AI legitimate and safe to use?


Remaker is an active browser service with an official[website](https://remaker.ai/) , published[terms](https://remaker.ai/en/terms-and-conditions/) , a[privacy policy](https://remaker.ai/en/privacy-and-cookies-policy/) , pricing, and[API documentation](https://remaker.ai/docs/api/) . Those are useful identity and policy checks; they are not the same as an independent security audit or a guarantee that every upload is suitable for sensitive work.


Before uploading a face, review the terms for the exact workflow. Remaker’s[browser photo FAQ](https://remaker.ai/face-swap-free/) says uploaded and generated images are deleted within 48 hours. Its[photo API documentation](https://remaker.ai/docs/api/face-swap/) separately says generated API images are deleted after 24 hours. These are different vendor-stated scopes, not a verified deletion test. The broader[privacy policy](https://remaker.ai/en/privacy-and-cookies-policy/) also describes account, billing, usage and advertising data; a short image-retention promise does not cover all of those records. Confirm the applicable workflow before uploading confidential material, and use only images you have permission to process.


**Remaker’s refund sources disagree.** Its[Terms and Conditions](https://remaker.ai/en/terms-and-conditions/) describe conditional first-purchase refunds: no more than 50 credits used and a request within three days, with approval not guaranteed. The[loaded pricing FAQ](https://remaker.ai/pricing/) instead says Crypto and Telegram Stars payments are non-refundable. The pricing screen offers “Card via Telegram” and Crypto, while its FAQ says direct card payments are unsupported. These are published statements checked October 21, 2026, not a completed checkout or refund test. Confirm the applicable payment route and refund policy with Remaker before paying; do not assume the terms’ eligibility conditions establish a refundable purchase.


## **A Note on Safe and Legal Use**


Use source media and likenesses you have permission to edit and publish. Do not present a manipulated performance as an authentic recording of what someone said or did. Check the disclosure requirements of the platform where you will share it; a tool subscription does not provide rights to third-party footage or people’s likenesses.

## A faster Remaker-to-Magic-Hour migration test


Do not rebuild the entire project first. Export one representative source face and one target that includes the hardest condition in the job: a profile turn, glasses, hair across the face, fast movement, or several people. Run that same pair in both services. Keep framing, duration, and source resolution constant so the comparison measures the workflow rather than different inputs.


**For a photo, judge identity, hairline, jaw, skin tone, and changes outside the face. For video, also inspect every turn, occlusion, cut, and lighting change.** Record attempts, credits consumed, processing time, cleanup time, export conditions, and whether the result is usable. Cost per accepted output is more useful than price per generation.


If the sample passes, move the rest of the project. If it fails, change one input variable before buying more credits. This preserves the parts of the Remaker workflow that already work while testing whether Magic Hour improves the exact deliverable you need.
